title: Government's Actions Following Auditor-General's Findings of Document Alterations and Irregularities for FY2020/2021
what_it_is: Government's Actions Following Auditor-General's Findings of Document Alterations and Irregularities for FY2020/2021

sections.label: Auditor-General irregularities questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about action on irregularities in the AGO report, investigations, individuals involved, and action against officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) what action does the Government intend to take with respect to irregularities found in audited documents reported in the Report of the Auditor-General for FY2020/2021 where documents were altered, backdated, artificially created and falsified by officers across three Ministries and two Statutory Boards; (b) how many investigations have been undertaken arising from these irregularities; (c) how many individuals are involved for each Ministry and Statutory Board; and (d) what specific action has been taken against officers in cases where investigations have concluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) in the past five years, what are the types of recurring themes for issues flagged out by the AGO; (b) which are the Ministries and agencies that are repeatedly flagged out by the AGO; (c) why do these lapses and violations keep recurring; and (d) what action is taken to prevent their recurrence.

sections.label: Six agencies recurring lapses
sections.summary: Six agencies were mentioned in Auditor-General's reports over five years for recurring lapses in procurement, contract management and IT controls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the past five years, six agencies have been mentioned in the Auditor-General’s reports for recurring lapses, mainly in the areas of procurement and contract management, and IT controls.

sections.label: Implementation deadlines for systems
sections.summary: One measure will cover about 800 high priority systems by December 2022 and all applicable systems by December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The former will be implemented for about 800 high priority systems by December 2022 and all applicable systems by December 2023, while the latter will be implemented for all applicable systems by December 2023.

sections.label: MCCY officers fabricated claims records
sections.summary: Two MCCY officers admitted fabricating claims records; investigations verified claims were valid, and officers received warnings affecting performance assessments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Five agencies were highlighted by AGO for possible irregularities in records furnished for audit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Two MCCY officers admitted to fabricating claims records for services rendered by external parties as the officers could not locate the records when requested by AGO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, the investigation verified that the claims were valid and the services were in fact rendered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The officers were issued official warnings and their performance assessments were affected.
